title: Cherry and Rosemary Focaccia
changes_from_base: No-knead potato-flake dough on a large tray, topped with cherries cooked in pomegranate molasses, with rosemary.
summary: A no-knead tray focaccia topped with cherries cooked down with pomegranate molasses, plus rosemary and flaky salt.
equipment: cling film or a clean tea towel

ingredients.item: fresh sweet cherries, pitted and halved

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Mix the flour, potato flakes, yeast, sugar, salt, 2 tbsp oil and lukewarm water briefly into a rough ball. Cover and leave 3 h, until doubled; there is no need to knead or fold. Potato flakes make the crumb tender and moist.

steps.title: Cherries
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the cherries 3 min, until they start to bleed juice. Add the pomegranate molasses and water and bubble 2-3 min, until syrupy and clinging to the fruit. Cool.

steps.title: Tray
steps.text: Spread 1 tbsp oil over the tray and push the dough out to the edges, leaving it 10-15 min whenever it shrinks back.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Brush the dough with the last 1 tbsp oil, then scatter over the cherries and their syrup, the rosemary and the flaky salt. Cover and leave 1 1/2 h.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Towards the end, heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan). Bake 20-25 min, until golden brown and crusty at the edges; the centre reads about 96 °C. Cool 10 min before cutting into 12.

tips: Frozen or drained tinned cherries work out of season.
Cook the cherries only until syrupy; overcooked fruit collapses on the bread.
If the dough keeps shrinking, rest it and stretch again instead of tearing it.
storage: Eat within 1 day at room temperature, or keep in the fridge for up to 3 days and warm at 180 °C for 5 min. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
